newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks sink as EMU doubts resurface.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks sink as EMU doubts resurface.

text.p: Madrid shares ended sharply lower on Monday, as another wave of doubts over the future single European currency hit the bourse, dealers said.
The outlook was seen volatile, although expectations of a fresh fall in the May inflation rate should underpin prices.
The general index fell 7.96 points, 1.38 percent, to 566.99 and the Ibex dropped 104.69 points, 1.58 percent, to 6,511.46.
The biggest stocks took the brunt of losses after recent rises. Telefonica shed 105 pesetas to 4,235, while Endesa sank 240 pesetas to 11,300.
BBV bucked the trend ahead of its July share split, adding 50 pesetas to 11,100.

Traders started selling on news that France requested more time to reflect on a plan to maintain budget stability after the single European currency is launched, casting doubt on the whole project, they said.

"Volatility is likely to continue to set the tone for the rest of this year, and any type of (single currency) comment like this will send the market lower, although the base is firm," said one dealer.
